patch.value: Durable loop continuation: idempotent resume, controller lease, cancellation drills

Make the persisted recursive loop durable and crash-safe. pm rl loop run becomes idempotent: re-running after a crash at ANY phase (collect, train, evaluate, promote) never double-counts the sample budget, never re-promotes, and never loses an artifact; every partially persisted generation is completed from its persisted evidence. Add pm rl loop status <id> (read-only reconstruction) and pm rl loop resume <id> (resume from the persisted programme). Two controllers racing to launch the same loop produce exactly one job: the launch is guarded by the pm SDK's own primitives — an owner-bound claim on the loop seed plus the SDK workspace lock (acquireLock), with dead-holder takeover — never an invented lock file; proven by a real two-process test. SIGINT/SIGTERM/AbortSignal mid-phase leave consistent state that a resume completes to the identical uninterrupted result.

pm rl loop run re-run after an injected failure at each phase boundary completes to the exact uninterrupted report, with one create per item in history and no duplicated metric events; pm rl loop status reports per-generation phase, consumed budget and terminal reason without mutating anything; pm rl loop resume completes an interrupted loop from the persisted seed configuration; two concurrent controller processes produce exactly one seed, one run per generation and one promotion, the loser failing with a stable contention error; a killed controller's lease is taken over promptly via dead-pid detection; AbortSignal/SIGTERM cancellation mid-phase stops at a phase boundary, leaves consistent state, and a subsequent resume completes the loop

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Starting the durable-continuation slice on branch feat/durable-rsi-continuation. Design decisions recorded as I go: (1) launch mutual exclusion uses the pm SDK's own primitives — an owner-bound claim on the loop seed item plus the SDK workspace lock acquireLock per generation, with dead-pid takeover of an abandoned SDK lock record; no invented lock file. (2) resume reconstructs state from persisted items only: the deterministic bandit receipt is recomputed and verified against the stored training configuration, and missing metric-event suffixes are appended rather than re-collected. (3) pm rl loop run becomes idempotent end to end; the previous loop_already_started refusal is replaced by resume semantics, while a different configuration under the same loop id still conflicts through the content-addressed registration identity.

value.author: codex-sol-review
value.text:
Read-only review by codex-sol-review for pm-rl-od32. Read pm context/search/list-open, pm get pm-rl-od32 and pm get pm-rl-apvf; reviewed index.ts, lm.ts, test/durable-loop.test.ts and test/lm-loop.test.ts. This is a static review of actively changing implementation, not final-head acceptance. Initial index.ts had the long identity-based lease; a later read includes controllerMutex/guard and the 60-second lease. Latest observed index.ts digest: 7be64575f3226821fee0ce3014ef3c19a1813cef8dc59dcba3a6393abe559b14. Named functions below remain the anchors as lines change.

P1 - Capture the acquired token before releasing the acquisition mutex. In index.ts acquireControllerLease, releaseRecovery runs before launch-authority initialization and before the read that sets token. If controller A stalls there beyond expiry, B can replace the lease; A then reads B's token and its guard accepts B's authority. Capture and validate a nonempty token from A's acquired SDK record while still under the mutex; never refresh a controller's expected token from a later disk read. Keep launch-authority mutations under this same fencing discipline.

P1 - Fence every mutation at its commit boundary, not only the entry check. Latest observed guard calls cover preparation, seed release, cancellation comment and terminal report, but executePendingGeneration still creates runs, appends notes, closes runs, publishes checkpoints, registers candidates, records refusals and promotes without guard. A holder displaced while paused at onPhase can resume those effects. Include promotion's in-lock read/check/write, and do not convert loop_lease_lost or lock contention into a permanent promotion refusal. Serialize takeover, renewal, publication and cleanup under one SDK mutex with fixed lock order, or use a sink-enforced token/epoch CAS. A standalone assertOwned followed by an awaited write has a check-to-use race. SDK lock release checks its token; the seed claim needs the same invocation-level fencing, especially when both controllers use the same PM author.

P1 - Renewal must be atomic and crash recoverable. The new guard writes the lease directly with writeFile, which truncates before replacing the content. SIGKILL during renewal can leave empty/partial JSON; controllerExpiry becomes invalid and acquisition refuses even explicit takeover. Reuse the temporary-file publication pattern under the mutex and preserve the acquired token. expireDeadControllerMutex also rewrites an inode in place: test a crash between write/truncate and subsequent recovery. A phase mutex with a billion-second lifetime that refuses takeover of a live/unverifiable holder protects safety but prevents bounded recovery of a hung holder during its guarded operation; state that availability limit or move long computation outside the commit mutex and reject late results at publication.

P1 - PM receipts alone cannot eliminate the effect-to-receipt window. In index.ts completeGenerationEvidence/executePendingGeneration, fitting and evaluation finish before checkpoint publication and Generation registration. A crash after compute or artifact publication but before the receipt reruns the work and remeasures wall_ms, potentially changing the wall-limit verdict. Use a stable per-generation/per-step input identity binding programme digest, trainer version, source checkpoint, collection digest and derived step configuration. Store immutable completed step results plus required metadata, then reference them in PM; reconcile a published result missing its PM receipt before executing again. A crash before durable result publication can still require repeating pure computation; do not claim exactly-once execution from PM receipts. Likewise, a crash after promotion's body update but before close currently leaves promoted=true that inspectCandidateVerdict accepts as complete. Recovery should finish the recorded promotion outcome/close without spending approval twice, rather than treating that partially applied operation as a fresh promotion.

P2 - Recovery and status currently execute completed LM work. inspectLmGeneration always calls lmCollectBatch, including before discovering no Run or an exhausted budget. verifyStoredLmGeneration calls executeLmStep, repeating fit/evaluation; executePendingGeneration recomputes them even when pending.item already exists. The new lm.ts restore helpers are useful but are not yet wired into those paths in the reviewed snapshot. Status/resume should validate receipt identities, checkpoint bytes, dataset/step linkage and exact event completeness without collect/train/evaluate calls. Validate duplicated, missing, reordered and foreign events when removing deterministic replay. Cache/restore the frozen base too: parseLmLoopConfig currently performs pretraining on every run/resume/status, before acquiring the execution lease.

P2 - Synchronous CPU phases delay cancellation and renewal. lmCollectBatch, trainLmStep, evaluateLmStep and pretraining do not yield or consume AbortSignal; timer renewal and OS signal handlers cannot run during their work. Use a worker or bounded yielding chunks with deadline/cancellation checks; fence result adoption even after cancellation. Persist a fully completed result before acknowledging cancellation so resume can reuse it. Check cancellation before new work and after each separately persisted collect/train/evaluate phase; train/evaluate callbacks currently both occur after the combined candidate is registered.

Missing evidence in test/durable-loop.test.ts and test/lm-loop.test.ts: phase-hook exceptions execute finally and are not hard crashes inside effect/receipt writes; existing takeover drills kill the old holder without letting it continue after replacement. Add separate counters proving zero completed collect/train/evaluate calls on status/resume; SIGKILL around result publication, PM receipt writes and promotion body/close; expired live-holder takeover followed by old-holder continuation; same-author stale cleanup; acquisition-token capture race; truncated renewal recovery; and real cancellation during CPU work. Match resumed reports to an uninterrupted reference, including accounting and wall-limit policy, rather than only comparing repeated resumed reports.

Tests: no test commands run; static code/test review only. Only this review comment is authored; no claim/status/release/close changes, no source edits, no commits or pushes, no PR action, no changes to pm-rl-9nlg or external System One receipt logic. Open risks above remain for implementation and orchestrator verification. STOP.
